questions.q: What act constituted the first human disobedience in the Garden of Eden?
options: Killing animals for food
Building a tower to reach heaven
Eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
Fighting with each other
questions.explain: The first act of disobedience occurred when Adam and Eve ate from the **tree of the knowledge of good and evil**, explicitly violating God's command in Genesis 2:17.

questions.q: Who deceived Eve into eating the forbidden fruit?
options: Adam
The Serpent
An Angel
Cain
questions.explain: According to **Genesis 3:1-5**, the **serpent** deceived Eve by twisting God's words and convincing her that she would not die if she ate the fruit.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What was the consequence of disobedience specifically pronounced upon the serpent in Genesis 3:14?
options: It would be cast into a lake of fire.
It would crawl on its belly and eat dust all the days of its life.
It would lose its voice forever.
It would become the servant of Adam.
questions.explain: God cursed the serpent, saying: 'Upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life' (**Genesis 3:14**).
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: As a consequence of the first disobedience, what punishment was given to the woman? (Genesis 3:16)
options: She would be banished to the desert.
She would experience multiplied pain in childbearing.
She would lose her ability to speak.
She would turn into a pillar of salt.
questions.explain: To the woman, God said: 'I will surely multiply your pain in childbearing; in pain you shall bring forth children' (**Genesis 3:16**).
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What punishment did God declare upon the man (Adam) for his disobedience? (Genesis 3:17-19)
options: He would never be able to eat fruit again.
The ground was cursed, and he would eat bread by the sweat of his face until he returned to the dust.
He would become a wanderer on the earth like Cain.
He would be blind for the rest of his life.
questions.explain: God told Adam that because he listened to his wife and ate the forbidden fruit, the ground was cursed, and he would have to toil and **sweat for his food** until death (**Genesis 3:17-19**).

questions.q: Immediately after eating the forbidden fruit, what was the first realization Adam and Eve had?
options: They realized they were naked and felt ashamed.
They realized they possessed all of God's power.
They realized the garden was shrinking.
They realized they could fly.
questions.explain: **Genesis 3:7** states: 'Then the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'disobedience' in a Christian context?
options: Failing an examination at school
Refusing or failing to obey God's laws and instructions
Having a disagreement with a friend
Accidentally breaking a valuable item
questions.explain: In Christian teaching, **disobedience** specifically means the intentional refusal or failure to follow the rules, laws, and instructions given by God or constituted authority.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Just as the first human disobedience brought consequences, disobedience to school rules and parents today often leads to ____________.
options: promotions and awards
immediate wealth
punishments and broken trust
automatic forgiveness without correction
questions.explain: Every act of disobedience has consequences. In modern contexts like school or family, disobedience results in **punishment, discipline, and broken trust**, reflecting the principle seen in Genesis.
